newsitem.title: USA: Advanta to report earnings below prior expectations.
newsitem.headline: Advanta to report earnings below prior expectations.

text.p: Consumer financial services company Advanta Corp. said Monday it plans to report 1997 results well below previous expectations, news that helped drag the stock down by almost 25 percent.
The company, based in Spring House, Pa., also said its chief operating officer had resigned and his responsibilities were being assumed by Chief Executive Alex Hart.

Additionally, Advanta said it hired Wolfensohn & Co. to assist in a review of its business strategy, growth prospects and operating environment aimed at improving Advanta's value for shareholders and other constituents.
Advanta's stock fell $9.8125 to $29.875 in morning trading on Nasdaq on active volume of more than 27 million shares.

The company, which provides consumers and small businesses with credit cards, mortgages, leases, insurance and deposit products to nearly six million customers, has more than $19 billion in managed assets and more than 3,500 employees.

For the first quarter the company said it expects a loss in the area of $20 million, or about 44 cents a share, compared with earnings of $41 million, or 91 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.
First Call estimated 1997 first quarter earnings at $1.03.
Advanta said that factors for the decline include continuing increases in consumer bankruptcies and charge-offs and lower receivable balances than originally expected in its credit card business.
The company said that its mortgage, leasing and insurance businesses continued to perform very well.
The company said it currently expects to report a net profit for full-year 1997, with estimated earnings of about $1.50 per share.
First Call estimated Advanta earnings at $4.37 for the year. In 1996, Advanta said it earned $3.89 per share.
Advanta also said Alex "Pete" Hart, its chief executive officer, has assumed the additional responsibilities of David Brooks, its chief operating officer, who resigned.

Separately, Standard & Poors lowered its ratings on Advanta Corp., Advanta National Bank USA, Advanta National Bank, and Advanta Capital Trust 1 and placed the ratings on CreditWatch with "developing" implications.
These rating actions follow the announcement that Advanta retained Wolfensohn & Co. to evaluate strategic alternatives, S & P said.
Fitch Investors Service also downgraded Advanta Corp.'s senior debt to BBB from A- and Advanta National Bank and Advanta National Bank USA's senior obligations to BBB+ from A.
